Measured while building #397 and left unfixed there, because the lever is outside what #397 may change.

## What was measured

`docs/evaluation/editorial-397/` (on the branch `kntnt-orchestrate/main/397` until it is integrated) re-ran #383's method on `claude-opus-5-5`. After #397's change no run writes a standfirst, a subheading or a call to action into the four #362 drafts, and `R1` is met on six of the eight post-change draft runs. The two that miss are the second run on each column draft, and both miss on one thing: a headline the column had, reworded on a finding under the headline contract.

- `post-column-sv-r1-b`: `Mallen har en ruta för allt utom poängen` became `Bibliotekets mötesmall har rutor för allt utom poängen`, on the finding *Rubriken förstods inte fristående*. The change of `en ruta` to `rutor` is not reported and breaks the column's recurring *en ruta*.
- `post-column-sv-r2-b`: `Rutan som inte finns` became `Bibliotekets mötesmall har ingen ruta för mötets syfte`, on the finding *Rubriken var otydlig*. Both judges record *syfte* as a change of meaning against the body's *beslut*.

Both judges of both runs class the rewrite as taste on a working headline under *clean texts may not be rewritten to satisfy taste*. The first run on each draft left the same headline alone, or attempted the rewrite and had its own re-review reject it. The pre-change arm reworded the headline in all four draft runs, among its other changes.

## Why this is not #397

The finding each run acts on is in `headlines.review.md`'s *Avoid* list — vague wording that needs the text to be understood. #397's readiness addendum keeps `headlines.md` and `headlines.review.md` unchanged, and #397's rule concerns parts a text lacks and bands. A signed column's allusive headline, whose referent the first paragraph supplies, is where the headline contract's *understood on its own* and the judges' reading of a working headline part.

## The open question

Whether a finished text's headline that the body resolves in its first lines fails *understood on its own*, or is a working headline the review leaves alone, and where that line is written for a reviewer.

`R1` on the four #362 drafts, both runs of each column draft, re-measured with #397's method, is the criterion a fix would be read against.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

This comment is the requirement wherever it touches the body. It also takes over #430 (the `article-clean` and `column-clean` headline rewrites) and the opinion half of #436 (the `opinion-en_GB-r1` subheading), which are closed as duplicates of this ticket. Thomas settled the open question on 2026-09-28: **on a finished text, Redline leaves a heading that works, and rewrites one only where a reader would be misled or lose something it can name.**

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Draw the line between a working heading and a heading finding where the reviewer reads it, so Redline stops rewriting headings that work.

**Current behaviour:**
`headlines.review.md` says each item on its *Avoid* list "is a finding" and, separately, that "a working headline is left alone", with no test that separates the two. So the review treats these as findings and rewrites them:
- an allusive headline that still tells the reader what the text is about (`Mätförsöket i Björkskolan visar när, inte varför`, `Mallen har en ruta för allt utom poängen`);
- a figure of speech in a column's own voice (`Mötesmallen har en ruta för allt utom varför`, read as an overclaim);
- a subheading that states its section's point, or shares topic words with the sentence under it (`Six months, both routes, and something to measure`);
- a subheading that "describes only the section's first paragraph" (`En gräns för det lokala försöket`).

The blind judges class every one as taste on a working heading. The rewrites also carry costs of their own:
- a changed meaning (`syfte` for the body's `beslut`);
- a broken recurring motif (`en ruta` → `rutor`);
- a false reason given for the change (*repeated the first sentence under it in the same words*).

On installs from 2026-09-24 onward, `article-clean`'s headline was rewritten in 4 of 9 runs and `column-clean`'s in 3 of 9. Both came back unchanged in #383's and #386's runs.
The evidence is in:
- `docs/evaluation/editorial-397/results.md`, target table and controls;
- `docs/evaluation/editorial-400/results.md`, *Misses no ticket above owns*;
- `docs/evaluation/editorial-402/runs/*-control-article-clean` and `*-control-column-clean`.

**Desired behaviour:**
A heading on the text under review is a finding only where the review can name what a reader of that heading loses. That is the case where the heading:
- claims more than the text, or something other than it;
- is louder in tone than the text;
- says again, in substance, what stands under it;
- gives away the point of a quotation under it;
- is a bare label or subject where the text has an angle, or a question where the text answers it;
- uses words the audience does not know;
- leaves a reader who sees only the heading unable to tell what the text is about.

The following are working headings and are left alone:
- an allusion or image that still tells such a reader what the text is about;
- a figure of speech in the text's own register, which is an overclaim only where a reader would take it as a factual claim the text does not support;
- a subheading that states what its section says;
- a heading that shares names or topic words with the sentence under it while saying something that sentence does not.

Where the review does repair a heading, the repair keeps the text's recurring words and figures and its meaning, which `column.review.md` and `headlines.review.md` already require.

The *Avoid* list stays a list (Thomas's #382 ruling). What changes is the guidance that tells the reviewer where an item stops applying. The line goes where the reviewer reads it: `headlines.review.md`'s *Leave alone* and its closing paragraph, and the review step and correction brief wherever they restate heading authority. `headlines.md`, the half /write loads, is not loosened. Write keeps aiming at the full rules. A limit on findings belongs in the review half, since it is guidance a writer has no use for (the editorial README's pair test).

**Key interfaces:**
- `headlines.review.md`: the *Avoid* list's opening sentence and the *Leave alone* section.
- Redline's step 6 heading-pair instruction and the correction brief's heading instruction. Both already say that shared topic words alone create no finding. Keep them consistent with the new line, and do not restate it three times.
- `genres/column.md`'s evocative-headline sentence, which must not contradict the new line.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The review half states, operably for a reviewer, where a heading stops being a finding, covering allusion, a figure of speech in the text's register, a subheading stating its section, and shared words. It does so without deleting or rewording any *Avoid* item.
- [ ] Nothing /write loads is loosened. `headlines.md` states the same requirements as before.
- [ ] Measured under a plan frozen before the first run, on `claude-opus-5-5` at high deliberation:
  - Arms: a fresh pre-change arm and the candidate.
  - Clean controls: at least three runs per arm on each of `article-clean`, `column-clean`, `case-study-clean` and `opinion-clean`, the latter two as #431 revised them. Each clean control is run as the protocol's response-target and file-target pair.
  - Drafts: two runs per arm of `column-sv-r1`, `column-sv-r2` and `opinion-en_GB-r1`.
  - Judges: two blind judges per run, using `docs/evaluation/editorial-397/control-judge-brief.md` and `redline-judge-brief.md`.
  - The plan fixes the bands in advance, as `docs/evaluation/editorial-399/plan.md` did.
- [ ] **Target:** in the candidate arm, no clean control comes back with a heading rewritten, and `R1` on the three drafts fails on no heading rewrite. Where one arm alone cannot show this, the plan's bands decide.
- [ ] **Controls:**
  - `article-flawed`, `case-study-flawed`, `column-flawed` and `opinion-flawed` still get their named heading defects repaired or reported, as their rows require.
  - #396's subheading-over-quotation finding still fires on `docs/evaluation/editorial-364/runs/b/case-question-en_GB-r2` and `-r3`.
- [ ] The result is written down as measured, in `docs/evaluation/editorial-429/`, with a record in `docs/evaluation/records/`. Each remaining miss is filed as its own `needs-triage` issue naming this one.
- [ ] The four checks in `CONTRIBUTING.md` pass, and the catalog is regenerated.

**Staging:** as `docs/evaluation/protocol.md` states it once #439 has landed. Until then, use the shared evaluation clause in #396's readiness addendum (seat, fresh pre-change arm, not-reproduced exit, one revise round, whose miss, `git archive` staging, where it goes, interrupted runs), with this ticket as the evaluation number.

**Out of scope:**
- `headlines.md` and anything else /write loads.
- The corpus. #431 revises the two controls that break later rules, and this ticket is blocked by it.
- Whole-round rejection (#433 and #389).
- The reply's incidental statements (#435).
- `web-copy`, which does not link the headline contract (#432).

**Blocked by:** #431, because two of this ticket's controls fail for reasons only #431 fixes. Also #439. Both edges are written to the tracker's native relation.

> *This was generated by AI during a readiness check.*

## Readiness addendum — 2026-09-28

`/ready-for-agent-check`'s method read this ticket in a context that did not write it, against `e1d248d9`, and found that a builder could not carry it alone. The blocking gap is how a judge sees the text a file-target run delivers. There are also a dozen smaller gaps in the product wording and the evaluation. This comment **voids what it amends**. Wherever it touches the body or the triage comment of 2026-09-28, this comment is the requirement. Everything it does not touch stands, and Thomas's ruling in the triage comment stands untouched: **on a finished text, Redline leaves a heading that works, and rewrites one only where a reader would be misled or lose something it can name.**

### Who builds this

This ticket is built in a Claude Code session, because the measurement is Claude-family and `docs/evaluation/protocol.md`'s *Provider isolation* forbids a Codex session from starting a Claude Harness or model. A builder that finds itself on any other Harness stops before the first run and says so, naming this sentence.

### Corrections to stale wording

- The body says the #397 evidence is "on the branch `kntnt-orchestrate/main/397` until it is integrated". That branch is gone. The evidence is on `main` under `docs/evaluation/editorial-397/`.
- The out-of-scope line "`web-copy`, which does not link the headline contract (#432)" refers to the installed genre `webcopy`. Since `4845c82f` the installed genres are spelled without a hyphen (`casestudy`, `webcopy`). Fixture and row IDs keep their hyphens (`case-study-clean`, `web-copy-clean`). The corpus README records this as *Revised for installed genre names* in `docs/evaluation/corpus/editorial-quality/README.md`.

### The product change

**The body's open question, and `Rutan som inte finns`.** The triage comment's ruling answers the body's open question. A heading is read as a reader who sees only the heading reads it. The body's first lines do not rescue a heading that leaves that reader unable to tell what the text is about. So:

- `Mallen har en ruta för allt utom poängen` (`column-sv-r1`) names the template. It is a working allusion, and rewriting it is a miss.
- `Rutan som inte finns` (`column-sv-r2`) does not tell a reader who sees only the heading that the column is about the library's meeting template. It falls under the seventh finding case, "leaves a reader who sees only the heading unable to tell what the text is about". A reader of it loses what the text is about, which is a loss the review can name. So a repair of it is licensed, and *Reading the target* below says how such a repair is counted.

The working-heading list is not widened to rescue this case.

**`headlines.review.md`, the *Avoid* section's opening sentence.** "Each of these in a headline or a subheading is a finding:" becomes the ruling's test. Each item below is a finding where the review can name what a reader of that heading loses. The triage comment's seven finding cases are **instances of that test, not an exhaustive list**. Its words "That is the case where the heading:" are read that way. An *Avoid* item they do not name stays a finding wherever that test holds. This covers "Partial quotes, colons in place of a verb, stilted headline-speak", for example a colon that leaves the reader unable to tell who did what. Every *Avoid* item stays word for word, as criterion 1 of the triage comment requires.

**`headlines.review.md`, *Leave alone*.** This section gains the four working-heading cases of the triage comment, stated once:

- an allusion or image that still tells a reader who sees only the heading what the text is about;
- a figure of speech in the text's own register, which is an overclaim only where a reader would take it as a factual claim the text does not support;
- a subheading that states what its section says;
- a heading that shares names or topic words with the sentence under it while saying something that sentence does not.

**"Its closing paragraph".** The triage comment says the line goes in "`headlines.review.md`'s *Leave alone* and its closing paragraph". *Leave alone* is one paragraph and is also the file's last, so "its closing paragraph" is read as **the *Avoid* section's closing paragraph**, the one opening "Name what the reader loses, and repair by rewriting the headline alone". That paragraph gains one sentence: a repair keeps the text's recurring words and figures, and its meaning. The triage comment says `column.review.md` and `headlines.review.md` "already require" this. That is half true. `column.review.md` does ("rhetorical recurrence, pointed imagery"). `headlines.review.md` says only "from the text's angle and at the text's own strength". That is why the sentence is added here. `column.review.md` does not change.

**Redline `SKILL.md`, step 6.** Step 6's list of heading defects includes "wording the reader has to read on to understand", a restatement the triage comment's *Key interfaces* does not name. It is reworded to name the same defect by the new test: a heading from which a reader who sees only it cannot tell what the text is about. No other item in that list changes. The sentence carrying "names that part and the defect in it" stays, because `tests/test_kntnt.py` holds it in place. Step 6's sentence "Necessary repeated names or topic words alone create no finding; a paraphrased repeat can be a finding with little or no overlap." stays as it is. Step 6 does not restate the working-heading cases, which live in `headlines.review.md` alone.

**Files that do not change, and why:**

- **`references/correction.md`.** Its heading sentence ("Necessary repeated names and topic words can be legitimate … `shared_words` alone never authorizes a change or creates a finding") already agrees with the new line. The correction agent loads `headlines.review.md` itself.
- **`article-anatomy.review.md`.** Its closing sentence already says that "A subheading that describes clearly what its section is about meets its requirement". The new working case "a subheading that states what its section says" is written once, in `headlines.review.md`, which the anatomy sends every heading to. A candidate-arm rewrite of `article-clean`'s `En gräns för det lokala försöket` is a target miss like any other and is filed. It is not a reason to edit this file.
- **`genres/column.md`.** Its sentence "The headline may be evocative as long as it is still understood on its own and states this column's angle" agrees with the new line. It is in the half /write loads, so it does not change.
- **`help.md`.** Redline's `help.md` states no heading finding that the new line contradicts.

The product change touches `skills/kntnt/library/references/editorial/headlines.review.md`, `skills/editorial/redline/SKILL.md` and the regenerated `skills/kntnt/catalog.json`, and no other file under `skills/`.

### The evaluation

**Staging.** Staging follows the staging section #439 adds to `docs/evaluation/protocol.md`. #439 is a native blocker of this ticket, so that section is in the tree when this ticket is built. The triage comment's fallback, "Until then, use the shared evaluation clause in #396's readiness addendum", is **void**: #439 is a native blocker, so that branch can never be taken. This ticket's method is `docs/evaluation/editorial-397/plan.md` as `plan-amendment.md` beside it amends, with paths, seat and the evaluation number substituted. This ticket departs from that method and adds to the protocol only where this section says so. Every run is made with `docs/evaluation/editorial-388/harness/staged_run.py`, `--model=claude-opus-5-5 --effort=high`, with the input staged as `--input-name=input.md`. The pre-change arm is staged from the commit the build started from. The candidate arm is staged from the committed candidate. The corpus commit is the commit the build started from, which holds #431's revision of `case-study-clean` and `opinion-clean`.

**Genre names.** A copied invocation uses the installed genre names (`--genre=casestudy`). That is not a change of method. It sits beside the path and seat substitution the protocol permits. The *Redline controls* table's Genre column already carries the installed names at `e1d248d9`. An input that carries old `genre:` metadata is staged unedited, and the invocation names the installed genre instead. When Redline's step 8 then rewrites that metadata line to `casestudy`, the synchronisation is not a finding against the run.

**Runs, per arm.** The table is exhaustive. Both arms run every row, because "still" and the protocol's comparison both need a pre-change reading.

| Input | Invocation | Runs per arm | Judged by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `article-clean`, `case-study-clean`, `column-clean`, `opinion-clean` (clean controls) | the table's invocation with `--language=sv`: `/redline --genre=<genre> --language=sv --output=response input.md`, and its pair with `--output=output.md` | **three pairs each**, a pair being one response-target run and one file-target run, as the protocol's *A clean control* defines them. "At least three runs per arm" is read as three pairs. | two judges per run |
| `column-sv-r1`, `column-sv-r2`, `opinion-en_GB-r1`, staged from `docs/evaluation/editorial-362/runs/<draft>/redline/work/input.md` | `/redline --output=response input.md` (each draft carries its own `kntnt` map) | two each | two judges per run, `redline-judge-brief.md` |
| `article-flawed`, `case-study-flawed`, `column-flawed`, `opinion-flawed` | `/redline --genre=<genre> --language=sv --output=response input.md` | one each | two judges per run, `control-judge-brief.md` with the row's frozen expectation |
| #396's control: `docs/evaluation/editorial-364/runs/b/case-question-en_GB-r2/delivered.md` and `…/case-question-en_GB-r3/delivered.md` | `/redline --genre=casestudy --language=en_GB --output=response input.md` | one each | no judges: the builder reads it from the reply and any delivered text, as #397's plan permits for the presence of a report |

That is thirty-six runs per arm, seventy-two before any revise round.

**Judging a file-target run.** This settles the stop. Each file-target run is made with `staged_run.py --capture-output-name=output.md`, which copies the delivered `work/output.md` into the packet as `captured-output.md`. That run's judges get a neutral directory holding three files:

- `work/input.md`, from the packet's `supplied-input.md`;
- `work/output.md`, from `captured-output.md`;
- `response.md`, from `response.txt`.

They judge it with a copy of `docs/evaluation/editorial-397/control-judge-brief.md` that differs in two places:

- its sentence "Read exactly those two files" names the three files;
- it gains, after that paragraph, the sentence: *"In this run the Skill delivered its text to `work/output.md`. Every difference you list under heading 1 is between `work/input.md` and `work/output.md`, and R1's clause on clean texts is judged from that file alone, never from what the reply says it changed."*

This is a **deliberate change of method** made by this ticket. It is the only one beyond paths, seat and genre names. It is needed because the protocol's *A clean control* says the clean-text criterion "is judged only from the file the file-target run delivered", and #397's brief cannot see that file. The protocol lets a copied judge brief take path and seat substitution without counting as a change of method. This addition is more than that, so the frozen plan declares it as a change of method, with its reason, before the first run.

- **Response-target runs** of the same pairs are judged with the unchanged brief. In the record, a response-target entry that returned only a no-change status has its `R1` scored `skipped`, with the reason the protocol gives: no text was delivered, and the file-target entry answers the criterion.
- **A file-target run that leaves no `output.md`** is recorded as delivering none, with its `R1` `skipped` for that reason. That is a defect filed as its own issue.

**Splits.** Where two judges split, the rule in `docs/evaluation/editorial-397/plan.md` under *When `R1` is met* decides, for `R1` and `C1` alike.

**Reading the target.** This replaces the triage comment's "Where one arm alone cannot show this, the plan's bands decide." and "The plan fixes the bands in advance, as `docs/evaluation/editorial-399/plan.md` did." There are no bands. The counting rule below is frozen in the plan before the first run. It is read per fixture, in each arm.

- **A clean control** meets the target in an arm when none of its six runs in that arm rewrote a heading. A heading is rewritten when any headline or subheading line in the delivered text (the file-target run's `output.md`, or a text a response-target run delivered in its reply) differs from the input, or is removed or added. A difference both judges class as a mechanical correction does not count.
- **A draft** meets the target in an arm when no run of it misses `R1` on a heading rewrite. A run misses on a heading rewrite when it misses `R1` under the split rule and the passage deciding a failing verdict is a heading difference. `R1` misses on anything else are recorded, and the whose-miss rule applies.
- **The one exception is `Rutan som inte finns` on `column-sv-r2`.** A run's rewrite of that headline does not count as a target miss when two things hold: the new headline keeps the column's recurring *ruta* (as *ruta*, *rutan*, *rutor* or *rutorna*), and neither judge classes the change as a change to what a claim says. That holds even where a judge fails `R1` on it as taste, because Thomas's ruling puts that headline on the finding side. The judges are told nothing about this. They stay blind and judge with the brief as copied. The builder applies the exception when reading their verdicts, and `results.md` gives the judges' verdicts as written and says why a run was not counted. A rewrite that changes what a claim says, such as #397's *syfte* for the body's *beslut*, or one that drops *ruta*, is a miss.
- **The target is met** when every clean control and every draft meets it in the candidate arm.
- **Not reproduced.** Where the pre-change arm meets the target on every fixture, the result is recorded as not reproduced on this seat.

**Reading the controls.**

- **Flawed controls.** Each row's heading clauses are:
  - `article-flawed`: the headline "fails on truthfulness";
  - `case-study-flawed`: "two subheadings, neither describing its section, the second claiming a conclusion the note itself declines to draw";
  - `column-flawed`: the headline "names no subject of its own and … claims a change the column never makes";
  - `opinion-flawed`: "`Bakgrund` and `Diskussion`, which label the sections instead of describing them".

  A flawed control passes in an arm when the judges' answers under heading 3 of their brief, read by the split rule, record a finding in the reply that names each of its heading clauses. It passes whether the run repaired the heading or left it reported. `C1` is recorded too.
- **#396's control.** It fires on a run when the reply reports a finding that the subheading says what the closing quotation under it says. The subheadings are `Vale would use the schedule again for new jobs` on `-r2` and `Vale would allow an extra week for the status names` on `-r3`. It also fires when the reply changes that subheading and names that defect as the reason. "Still fires" is read against this evaluation's own pre-change arm, since no earlier Redline run measured it. #396's plan made no Redline run, and #364's paired runs predate #396's rule.
  - A draft on which the pre-change run fires and the candidate run does not is a regression.
  - A draft on which neither fires is recorded as such and filed as its own `needs-triage` issue naming #396 and this ticket. It is not counted against this ticket.

**Whose miss.** The protocol's rule applies. A miss caused by a behaviour another ticket was filed against is recorded under that ticket's number. That covers #433 (whole-round rejection), #435 (the reply's incidental statements) and #400 (a changed heading accounted for as something else), among others.

**What ships in each outcome.** Thomas ruled on this behaviour, so the change ships whatever the measurement shows. This is the maintainer's-ruling case of the protocol's *not reproduced* rule. The measurement decides only what is written down as met or missed and what is filed.

- **The target is met and no control regresses.** The candidate ships, recorded as met.
- **The target is missed, or a control that passed pre-change fails in the candidate arm.** The protocol's one revise round may be taken. Where it is, the wording that ships is whichever of the two candidates has fewer target misses over the re-run subset, or the first where they are level. Either way the change ships. Every remaining miss and every regression is recorded as measured and filed.
- **Not reproduced.** The candidate still ships, the candidate arm is still run and recorded, and no decision record is written for the non-reproduction.

No acceptance criterion falls away in any branch, because the criteria below ask for a reading recorded, not a reading met. No branch writes a decision record. The change is prose in a review half that one commit reverses, so it fails the first of `docs/rules/docs.md`'s three criteria. `results.md` says so.

**Filing.** Each remaining miss is filed as its own `needs-triage` issue naming #429, one issue per fixture whose reading missed in the candidate arm. A miss the whose-miss rule assigns to an open ticket is recorded under that ticket and not filed again.

### Acceptance criteria

This list **replaces every acceptance criterion in the triage comment**.

- [ ] `headlines.review.md`'s *Avoid* opening sentence states the ruling's test: an item is a finding where the review can name what a reader of that heading loses. It states it so that the seven finding cases read as instances rather than an exhaustive list. Every *Avoid* item is word for word as it was at the commit the build started from.
- [ ] `headlines.review.md`'s *Leave alone* states the four working-heading cases listed under *The product change*, once, operably for a reviewer: allusion or image, figure of speech in the text's register, subheading stating its section, and shared names or topic words.
- [ ] The *Avoid* section's closing paragraph says that a repair keeps the text's recurring words and figures and its meaning.
- [ ] Redline `SKILL.md` step 6's item "wording the reader has to read on to understand" names the defect by the new test. No other item in that list changes. Neither step 6 nor `references/correction.md` restates the working-heading cases.
- [ ] Nothing /write loads is loosened. Under `skills/`, the change touches only `headlines.review.md`, Redline's `SKILL.md` and the regenerated `catalog.json`, so `headlines.md` and `genres/column.md` state the same requirements as before.
- [ ] `docs/evaluation/editorial-429/plan.md` was committed before the first run. It records the method copied from `docs/evaluation/editorial-397/plan.md` and `plan-amendment.md`, the run table above, the file-target judge brief's change with its reason, and the counting rule under *Reading the target*. The copied briefs sit beside it.
- [ ] Every run in the run table was made in both arms on `claude-opus-5-5` at high deliberation through `staged_run.py`. Each file-target run was made with `--capture-output-name=output.md` and judged with the file-target brief. Every judged run has two blind judgements.
- [ ] `docs/evaluation/editorial-429/results.md` gives, for each fixture and arm, the target reading (met or missed, with the runs that decide it), each flawed control's heading-clause reading, #396's control's reading, and whether the defect reproduced. It names every run the `Rutan som inte finns` exception kept off the count, with both judges' verdicts. It states what shipped and why.
- [ ] A record, `docs/evaluation/records/redline-claude-<YYYY-MM-DD>-429.md`, is written in the protocol's format, with its entry for `docs/evaluation/records/README.md`. Each remaining miss is filed as its own `needs-triage` issue naming #429, and `results.md` lists their numbers.
- [ ] The four checks in `CONTRIBUTING.md` pass, and the catalog is regenerated with `KNTNT_SOURCE=. uv run skills/kntnt/scripts/kntnt.py catalog --write`.

## Readiness addendum 2 — 2026-09-29

A second reading by `/ready-for-agent-check`'s method, against `e1d248d9`, judged that a builder can carry this ticket alone. It found that two of the four working-heading cases, written word for word, collide with *Avoid* items that stay word for word, and one of the collisions would regress #396's control. This comment settles that. It amends the triage comment and the readiness addendum of 2026-09-28, and **voids what it amends**. Everything else in both stands, and Thomas's ruling stands untouched: on a finished text, Redline leaves a heading that works, and rewrites one only where a reader would be misled or lose something it can name.

### The working-heading cases never override two *Avoid* items

The four cases the readiness addendum puts in *Leave alone* describe the shape of a heading that works. They do not license a heading that also meets either of these *Avoid* items in `skills/kntnt/library/references/editorial/headlines.review.md`, which stay word for word:

- **Item 1**, *"Claims, figures, names or conclusions not found in the text. A headline that sharpens, generalises or draws a conclusion the text itself does not draw is always a finding, however well it reads."* A figure of speech in the text's own register is working only where a reader would not take it as such a claim. That is already how the triage comment worded the figure-of-speech case. Where a reader would take it as one, item 1 decides.
- **The item on a subheading over a quotation**, *"A subheading that pre-spends the judgement, figure or concession of a quotation standing under it …"*, together with `headlines.md`'s *A subheading over a quotation*. The case *"a subheading that states what its section says"* is working **only where the section's point is not a quotation's judgement, figure or concession**. Where it is, the subheading names the subject, the occasion or the speaker and leaves the point to the quotation, as the existing last sentence of *Leave alone* already says. A subheading that states that point pre-spends the quotation and stays a finding.

So *Leave alone* states the four cases with these two bounds, once, in the same place. #396's control subheadings (`Vale would use the schedule again for new jobs` on `case-question-en_GB-r2`, and `Vale would allow an extra week for the status names` on `-r3`) state the point of the quotation under them. They stay findings, and the control keeps firing.

### Acceptance criteria

This amends the readiness addendum's second criterion. It now reads:

- [ ] `headlines.review.md`'s *Leave alone* states the four working-heading cases once, operably for a reviewer: allusion or image, figure of speech in the text's register, subheading stating its section, and shared names or topic words. It bounds them so that none overrides *Avoid* item 1 (a claim the text does not support, as a reader would take it) or the item on a subheading that pre-spends a quotation. A subheading stating its section is working only where the section's point is not a quotation's judgement, figure or concession.

Every other criterion of the readiness addendum stands. This comment adds no blocking edge.
